title: OIDC Hybrid Flow (code id_token)
subtitle: The IdP returns a code AND a front-channel ID token at once — the id_token’s c_hash binds the code so a stolen/substituted code can’t be redeemed.

steps.label: Visit a protected page
steps.lede: The user hits a protected page in a web app (the RP). The app stores state and nonce, then bounces to the IdP asking for both a code and a front-channel ID token.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log (the authorize redirect navigates away). Hybrid’s tell is response_type=code id_token: you get an ID token in the front channel and a code to redeem in the back channel.

steps.label: Redirect to /authorize (form_post)
steps.lede: The browser is redirected to the authorization endpoint. nonce is mandatory for hybrid. With response_mode=form_post the IdP returns an HTML page that auto-submits code + id_token + state to the callback.

resp.json:
<!doctype html>
<form method=post action="https://rp.example.com/cb">
  <input name=code value="SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA">
  <input name=id_token value="eyJ…front…">
  <input name=state value="abc">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit()</script>

steps.devtools: Filter on authorize. Confirm response_type=code id_token, state, and the mandatory nonce. If response_mode=form_post, the response is an auto-submitting HTML form (below) rather than a fragment redirect — much easier to read.

steps.label: form_post delivers code + front-channel id_token
steps.lede: The auto-submitted form POSTs code, the front-channel id_token, and state to the RP callback. The RP verifies state, validates the id_token, then confirms c_hash binds this exact code.

jwt.title: Decoded front-channel id_token (carries c_hash)
payload: Must equal the nonce you sent — replay binding

steps.devtools: Filter on cb. Read the Form Data: code, id_token, state. Decode the id_token and confirm nonce matches and a c_hash claim is present. (In default fragment mode the tokens would be after # in the address bar — not sent to the server — with the same leakage caution as implicit.)

steps.label: Validate id_token + verify c_hash
steps.lede: The RP fully validates the front-channel id_token (JWKS signature, iss, aud, exp, nonce), then recomputes base64url(left-half(SHA-256(code))) and compares it to c_hash. A match proves the code wasn’t substituted — the RP can start a session immediately.
steps.devtools: Not a network event. A c_hash mismatch means code injection/substitution — the RP must reject and never redeem the code at /token.

steps.label: Redeem code at /token (back-channel)
steps.lede: The RP back end POSTs the code to /token with client authentication and gets back an access token plus a SECOND id_token — this one richer, from the back channel.

jwt.title: Decoded back-channel id_token (second token)
payload: MUST equal the front-channel token’s iss
MUST equal the front-channel token’s sub
Issued a few seconds after the front-channel token
Richer claims than the front-channel token

steps.devtools: Not in the browser — this is the RP’s server-to-server call. Capture it on the RP if you need to see it. It returns a second id_token; the RP checks its iss/sub match the front-channel token.

steps.label: Cross-token consistency check
steps.lede: The RP compares the two ID tokens: iss and sub MUST be identical. If they differ, it discards the tokens and restarts authentication.
steps.devtools: Not a network event. This guards against a mismatched back-channel token being stitched onto a valid front-channel response — a mismatch means discard everything and re-authenticate.

steps.label: Call the API with the access token
steps.lede: With validated tokens, the RP calls the resource server presenting the access token as a Bearer credential. If the RP calls the API server-side, this is off-browser too.
steps.devtools: Filter on resource — but you’ll only see it here if the browser makes the call. A server-side RP performs this from its back end, invisible to DevTools. The resource server validates the Bearer token (JWKS, iss, aud, exp, scopes) before returning data.
